Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Pre-commit traffic inventory & sizing inputs — Aperture

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the time this morning. Per our call, to produce a defensible dedicated sizing recommendation we need a compact traffic inventory and a small sample of production telemetry. The goal is to validate occupancy assumptions (sessions vs. stateless requests), prompt/response length distribution, and burst characteristics for peak dayparting.

Please send:
- ~1 week of request-level telemetry (timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id if applicable, client_region) — CSV is fine.
- A short prompt mix doc describing the top 10 prompt templates and expected P95 response lengths.
- Any SLO constraints (p99 latency targets at token-level, acceptable tail percentiles).

If you prefer, attach a redacted sample (remove PII) — we only need structure and shape. I attached a template CSV to make this quick. Once we have that, Karthik and I will run a sizing probe and follow up with a short matrix: committed GPUs, burst pool sizing, expected token-economics.

Deliverable timeline: we can return an initial draft within 48 hours of getting the sample.

Thanks —
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Camila —

Thanks, that makes sense. Attaching a one-week sample from our US prod cluster and a brief prompt mix PDF. We redacted user IDs and stripped message bodies where there was PII. A couple of notes:
- Traffic is largely stateless API calls (search-style queries) for our recommendation widget ~85% of calls, with ~15% conversational sessions that reuse a session_id.
- Average prompt_tokens is ~30, median response_tokens ~120, but we see a heavy tail during marketing events where response_tokens hit 800–1200 for complex docs.
- Peak daypart: weekdays 11:00–14:00 PT; peak-minute QPS last month was 210.

Files attached: aperture_prod_telemetry_sample.csv, aperture_prompt_mix_v1.pdf

Let me know if you need a longer window. We'd like the draft sizing by Friday so we can align budget.

—Samir
Samir Patel, Dir. Product Operations, Aperture AI
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pre-commit traffic inventory & sizing inputs — Aperture

Karthik / Marissa —

Forwarding Samir's sample. Quick summary of the call and attached telemetry:
- Traffic shape: 85% single-shot requests, 15% session affinity.
- Token distribution: prompt median 30, response median 120, P95 ~780 (marketing spikes).
- Peak observed sustained QPS: 210 (peak-minute).

Asks for sizing probe:
1) Confirm occupancy model: for single-shot requests we should assume average lifetime = response_token * 1.5 ms per token on our target GPU (quantized config) — confirm if that maps to our kernel bench.
2) For sessions, we need to estimate KV cache hit rates; Samir doesn't have telemetry on KV reuse. Recommend we size conservatively assuming cold starts for 40% of session requests.
3) Burst pool approach: propose 25% burst capacity on top of committed GPUs to cover marketing spikes — ask Marissa to validate cost impact and an initial pricing calc.

Karthik: can you run the quick probe today (sample->occupancy estimate->committed+burst calc)? Marissa: can you draft a one-page margin and pricing impact on 3 commitment tiers (Small/Medium/Large)? We'll turn both into a short deliverable for Samir.

Camila
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-commit traffic inventory & sizing inputs — Aperture

Camila / team / Samir —

I ran a quick occupancy probe against the sample. High-level results (very rough, draft):
- Effective token processing latency assumption: 1.45 ms/token (quantized mix we benchmarked against A100-q8 profile).
- Estimated average request CPU/GPU lifetime: single-shot = 174 ms (~120 response tokens * 1.45 ms). Session requests with warm KV reduce per-request GPU time by ~22% when cache hit; since we assume 40% cold starts, net session-weighted lifetime ~155 ms.
- Baseline committed capacity options (to meet 99th p99 SLO target of 400ms):
  * Small: 4 G4-like GPUs (sustained ~150 QPS headroom) + 1 GPU burst (25% buffer) — expected P99 ~390ms during normal daypart, risk during marketing spikes.
  * Medium: 8 G4-like GPUs + 2 GPU burst — sustained headroom ~320 QPS, handles typical spikes with some margin.
  * Large: 12 G4-like GPUs + 3 GPU burst — comfortable for steady growth and marketing events.

Cost/back-of-envelope: Medium commitment reduces token unit cost by ~18% vs. Small when amortized over a monthly committed baseline; I'll hand off exact numbers to Marissa for pricing.

Next steps: Marissa to produce the pricing triangle + recommended fallback routing (model downgrades for non-critical requests during 90th–99th percentiles). Samir — if you can confirm whether marketing spikes are scheduled or ad-hoc, we can tune burst sizing.

Thanks —
Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
